HOW IT WORKS

Lower fees, in six steps.

  1. Connect your wallet. No account, no deposit. You trade straight from your own wallet.
  2. Swap on Exeswap. Exeswap finds the cheapest route for your trade, just like any aggregator. Fast, simple, convenient.
  3. Opt in to XPR for lower fees. It’s optional. Your verified on-chain signal determines your XPR – a number from 0.00 to 1.00 that acts as your personalized ‘exchange rate.’ Stronger signal, higher XPR.
  4. Higher XPR, lower fees. XPR is the share of each trade’s fee you can redeem from 0–100%. At Tier 1, XPR 0.40 redeems up to 40%. Same tier, XPR 1.00 redeems up to the whole fee.
  5. See it before you sign. Every quote shows the full fee, what your XPR pays and what you pay. Approve it, and that quote is fixed.
  6. Settled for you. Your trade is recorded the moment you approve it, then settled on-chain later in netted batches to keep costs down.

COMMON QUESTIONS

You asked, we answer.

Do I have to use XPR?
No. XPR is opt-in. Without it, Exeswap works as a regular aggregator: you get the cheapest route and pay the normal fee.
How is redemption funded?
First from your own fees: up to 70% of the protocol fee you paid. The rest comes from Exe’s pool, funded by the apps using Exe Protocol. Redemption never exceeds the fee you paid.
What is pool strength?
How much of what your XPR earns that Exe’s pool can pay right now. At 100% pool strength, you redeem everything your XPR earns. If Exe’s pool runs low, everyone’s share from the pool shrinks equally. The part paid from your own fees depends only on your XPR, never on pool strength.
What are tiers?
Tier 1 is where everyone starts. Tier 2 adds a budget commitment, earns more from the same XPR, and lets your XPR go up to 1.10. Tier 3 earns more again, so your fees stay low even in a quieter month.
How do I reach Tier 2?
Set aside a budget in your own wallet, usually about 10% (between 5% and 25%, lower for a long, steady history) of what you trade in a month. The budget stays in your wallet, and Exe Protocol never holds it. You can withdraw it at any time, and Tier 2 ends.
How do I reach Tier 3?
Stay at Tier 2 with an XPR of 0.75 or more for four months in a row. Two months below 0.75 and you move back to Tier 2.
Is this live?
Not yet. Every figure on this site comes from our simulation and is not a live price.

        Why did I get this?

          Sponsorship Pool

          The Sponsorship Pool, month by month

          Exe Protocol pays fee redemption from the Sponsorship Pool (SP, or ‘Exe’s pool’ for short), serving Exeswap users while keeping a separate account for each app. The Exeswap aggregator is Exe Protocol’s own app, so its 0.10% fee goes straight to Exe Protocol, with no extra app fee on top. That’s why fee redemption on Exeswap can cover the whole fee. Other apps may charge a fee of their own, which the ‘App funding’ section explains.

          Pool balancePool reserve (starts at $1.5M)Buffer $0.3M (never spent)

          When Exe’s pool holds more than its reserve, the surplus goes back to users the next month by raising the Fee Coverage Index (up to 2×). That lifts what Tiers 2 and 3 earn. Tier 1 earns exactly its XPR.

          Anything left after that is split. 70% of it grows the reserve, up to three months of fee redemption. The rest is held for $XPT buybacks, which stay off until legally cleared.

          When the pool is below its reserve, it pays out at most an eighth of what it can spend each month, and everyone’s share from the pool shrinks by the same proportion. The part from users’ own fees is always paid in full, whatever the pool holds, because that part comes from the fees themselves, not from Exe’s pool.

          Money in, fee redemption out

          A stress test, not a forecast. Every simulated user trades the same amount every month, so the lines run flat by design. What it shows: once settled, money in covers all fee redemption every month with a surplus left over, so the pool doesn’t run down in this test.

          Into the pool (70% of revenue: Exeswap fees + fees from other apps)Fee redemption paidSurplus (held for $XPT buybacks once legally cleared)

          Projection: if trading grows 8% a month

          Illustrative, not a forecast. The same users and the same rules, with their trading and the fees from other apps both growing 8% a month (about six times over two years). It shows the pool scaling with activity: redemption grows with it, and the pool stays funded.

          What smarter means

          Priced by signal

          Higher XPR, more of the fee redeemed. Exe Protocol redeems more of the fee for stronger signal.

          Funded by a shared pool

          First from the agent’s own fees, then from Exe’s pool, funded by protocol fees and the apps using Exe Protocol.

          Determined before it happens

          Pre-funded budgets, policy and tiers approve each payment at the quote. It’s designed so a rogue agent can’t spend beyond its budget.

          Settled net

          Only what each agent owes or is owed overall goes on-chain, so settlement grows with agents, not payments. One fingerprint per batch (a Merkle root) lets any agent check its own balance.

          Smarter is why it's faster and cheaper

          1. Strong verified signal, higher XPR. design
          2. More of each fee redeemed, from the agent's own fees and the shared pool. tested in simulation
          3. Rewarding the most valuable activity is designed to attract more of that activity. hypothesis: pilot
          4. More activity, more fees funding redemption, and netting saves more as payments per agent rise. simulated

          Faster: payments are set in advance by policy, not one by one at payment time. Cheaper: fees priced by signal, settlement netted.
